name: Supply chain and logistics
description: Supply, shipment and recall expertise for exercises: the terms and records buyers, planners, logistics managers and recall teams use, the decisions they make (allocate, switch source, reroute, hold, recall, notify) and the clocks they are measured on. Works for any organization that depends on goods: a hospital's materials office, a utility's spare parts, a retailer, a school's food service, a manufacturer. Stays at coordination level: lots, quantities, dates, ship-to lists, notices. Every company, carrier and customer is fictional.
outsideParties: suppliers at tiers one to three
carriers, freight forwarders and third-party logistics providers
the FDA or USDA FSIS and the state health department
the insurer and the trade press

advisorRoles.name: Supply chain adviser
advisorRoles.description: Answers questions about days of supply, allocation rules, lead times and alternate sources.

advisorRoles.name: Freight and port adviser
advisorRoles.description: Advises on lane, mode and port choices, dwell, detention and demurrage.

glossary.definition: On-hand plus confirmed inbound, divided by average daily demand. Stock-out date = today + days of supply.
The stock level at which a new order is placed: demand over lead time plus safety stock.
Tier 1 sells to the company; tier 2 sells to tier 1; tier 3 to tier 2. Hidden tier-2 dependencies are the usual surprise.
A contract clause excusing a supplier after an event outside its control; a letter claiming it starts a negotiation, not an answer.
Fees when a container stays at a terminal past free time (demurrage) or leaves it and is returned late (detention).
The identifier a firm assigns to a lot at its critical tracking events; shipping records carry it with quantity and unit, product, location, ship date and reference document (21 CFR 1.1340).
FDA: Class I serious harm or death is reasonably probable; Class II temporary or reversible harm; Class III unlikely to cause harm. Market withdrawal for minor violations.
How far down the chain the recall reaches: consumer, retail or wholesale level (21 CFR 7.42).
A: 100 percent of consignees; B: more than 10 and less than 100 percent; C: 10 percent; D: 2 percent; E: none (21 CFR 7.42(b)(3)).
A direct account that received the product. Notify each promptly; mark the letter urgent for Class I and II (21 CFR 7.49).

productConventions: A recall letter names the product, lot codes, reason, hazard, instructions and a way to reply; Class I and II letters are marked URGENT.
Shipment tables show lane, carrier, vessel or trailer, ETA, status and the exception reason.
A records request under FSMA 204 gives 24 hours or a reasonable time FDA agrees to; the output is an electronic sortable spreadsheet.
realismRules: Shipped quantity equals received plus in transit, and lot codes keep one format across a scenario's records.
Never state an FSMA 204 enforcement date as settled: the compliance date is subject to enforcement discretion until at least 2028-07-20.
Recall status reports go to the regulator every two to four weeks; the company may recall without waiting for FDA (21 CFR 7.46).
Use fictional companies, carriers and customers; no real brand names.

criticalTasks: Identify tier-2 and tier-3 dependencies for the affected item.
Assess supplier status and decide on an alternate source with its qualification status stated.
Keep records that let a lot be traced to every consignee.
State days of supply by item and site and the projected stock-out date.
Choose and state an allocation rule and apply it the same way to every customer.
Reroute or change mode with the cost and the new ETA stated.
Assign who contacts each supplier, carrier, customer and regulator.
Keep one list of consignees and one status for each shipment.
Notify direct accounts in a stated order and mark Class I and II recall letters urgent.
Decide on a public warning on the health hazard and state the basis.
Sequence the return to normal supply and lift allocation on a stated rule.
Record cost of expedite and lost sales for the after-action review.
